sources.title: Trading in the Sunshine or in the Shade: Market Impact and Adverse Selection on Hyperliquid
sources.finding: Visible TWAP executions were associated with smaller persistent displacement and more supplied liquidity than inferred hidden order sequences. The comparison is observational: execution method strongly depends on trader identity.
sources.scope_limit: Transaction sample spans July2025–March2026 across201markets; book snapshots are one-minute frequency. This does not validate100ms-to10s rules on Core/RH. Identifying continuing parent orders would require evidence beyond anonymous print size.

sources.title: The Neutrinos of the Order Book: Pervasive, Weakly Interacting Order Flow and its Consequences
sources.finding: The Hyperliquid BTC study uses complete message traffic, including rejected orders, and finds that much replenishment after spread widening was submitted before the widening occurred.
sources.scope_limit: Abstract inspected through primary SSRN indexed text; full manuscript not fetched. Our public snapshots omit rejected and in-flight orders. Observed book recovery cannot establish that a reactive retail order could capture the same opportunity.

sources.title: Order Flow Impact and Price Formation in Centralized Crypto Exchanges
sources.finding: For BTC on Coinbase and Binance, submissions and cancellations contribute substantially to price discovery, and very short-term cross-market discrepancies persist despite broader price integration.
sources.scope_limit: Abstract inspected through primary SSRN indexed text; direct fetch returned403. Different venues and assets. Suggests recording quote changes alongside prints; it does not identify a profitable Core/RH trade.

sources.title: Order flow and cryptocurrency returns
sources.finding: The study separates components of flow associated with reversal and persistence using daily and weekly cryptocurrency returns.
